Rescue Priority and Collateral Damage.text: Hero work has a clear order: save lives first, then contain the danger, then capture the villain. A hero who chases a suspect past trapped civilians is failing at the job even if the capture succeeds, and the academies, the Commission and the public all judge heroes by that rule. The social contribution score on the Hero Billboard Chart JP rewards evacuations and rescues as well as captures, and rescue specialists are respected for it. Fights between Quirk users break things. Buildings crack, cars burn, roads split and water mains burst, and the bill is real. Agencies carry liability insurance, the government covers some damage done in the course of lawful hero work, and a hero whose force was reckless or unnecessary can face claims, Commission discipline and a drop in approval. Mount Lady is known for the damage her size leaves behind, and heroes with large-scale Quirks train hard in precision for the same reason. Public anger follows visible damage quickly. Shop owners and residents complain to the press, news programs replay the wreckage, and online commentators argue over whether a hero went too far. The same footage can make a hero famous if it shows people carried out alive. Hero academies drill these choices in disaster exercises, rescue tests and mock-city battles, grading students on whom they saved and what they broke as well as on what they defeated.
